summary: Colville NF, Stevens County, WA summit; a camp from 1934, an L-4 tower of 1952 or 1938 that was removed or destroyed in the 1960s, and a hiking trail to the summit today.

facts.design: L-4 cab tower; FFLOS and Willhite say 20 feet (built 1952), FireLookout.com says 30 feet (1938)
facts.status_note: Tower removed in the 1960s per FFLOS and Willhite (FireLookout.com says destroyed). The summit is a hiking destination; the guide's photo caption points to stairs at the old footings.

access.note: Hikers reach the summit on Forest Service trail 117 (the guide gives 3.5 miles) from a small trailhead at the end of road 300; the road is single lane with ruts and is passable by passenger car, barely

visit.trail_note: Forest Service trail 117, which the guide gives as 3.5 miles, begins at a small trailhead at the end of road 300. The tower is gone, so there is nothing to climb.

events.note: Started as a fire lookout camp on the peak
FireLookout.com lists a 30-foot L-4 tower in 1938. A 1938 newspaper reports a carpenter working on a Forest Service lookout station that year; the sources do not say it was finished.
The Wagoner family staffed the lookout for the 1944 season, per Spokane Chronicle reports
20-foot L-4 tower built, per the FFLOS record and the Willhite climbing guide
Registered November 23, 2012 as US 1482, WA 382; nominated by Ray Kresek

resolved_conflicts.explanation: FireLookout.com gives a 30-foot L-4 tower in 1938; the FFLOS record and Willhite give a 20-foot L-4 tower built in 1952. Not resolved. The story gives both.
FFLOS and Willhite say the tower was removed in the 1960s; FireLookout.com says destroyed in the 1960s. Both are reported.

notes_for_editor: The brief's record is consistent with the sources; no corrections. Status is removed (no structure described as standing), and the summit is a public hiking destination per Willhite. The 1952 versus 1938 tower dates and the 20 ft versus 30 ft heights conflict and are not resolved; the 1938 newspaper confirms lookout construction work that year but not completion. No year is given for the removal, so no removal event is recorded (the schema needs a year). The 1944 staffing names are left out of the story beyond 'a man with the same surname'; the 1938 newspaper death is not mentioned. Access 'public' rests on a hiking guide, not an agency notice; an editor may want to check Forest Service access rules. Used 1 WebSearch and 5 page reads.
